<reason>PRO opened with a vivid, memorable frame (civic reserve turned into inventory; "privatizes the surplus and socializes the shortage") and correctly widened its own text to cover aquifer extraction, closing the first escape-hatch attack. But CON identified and repeatedly exploited the load-bearing weakness: the motion regulates owner identity, not litres. Three CON hits materially damaged PRO's route. First, the usufructuary answer — water rights are conditional permits curtailed in drought without litigation — directly undercut PRO's central story that the bottler "owns the well" and can fight cutoffs as property; PRO's reply was assertion ("still a claim that must be argued down") rather than mechanism. Second, the capture-symmetry contradiction: PRO said caps get lobbied hollow, yet exempts irrigated agriculture and, in [A4.4], expressly trusts caps to restrain farms, breweries and fabs. PRO's only escape was the input-vs-cargo distinction, which CON dismantled with the plausible, ordinary point that irrigation water also leaves the basin (in vapour and crops), making PRO's "shipped out of the cycle" harm theory point at users the ban exempts. Third, CON showed PRO's "sham reformulation" policing reimports the discretionary, lobbyable enforcement PRO had declared doomed. Pressure questions were well used on both sides with correct A1:/A2: labelling, but CON's answers were more direct and its questions produced the concession CON later monetised. PRO's local-concentration reply to "rounding error" was its best surviving line, yet CON's recharge-tied caps plus domestic-use-first drought priority plausibly cover it, and PRO never explained what the ban adds in litres once caps are conceded to work elsewhere. CON also gave the cleaner decision rule and stuck to it across rounds.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's exploitation of [A4.4]: by getting PRO to concede that volumetric caps would restrain farms, breweries and chip fabs, CON turned PRO's own capture argument into a "theory of villainy, not hydrology," then closed by showing the input-vs-cargo distinction is hydrologically empty since irrigation exports water from the basin too — leaving the ban buying "a feeling," not litres.</best_rebuttal>
